newsitem.title: INDONESIA: BADMINTON-SUSANTI WINS GRAND PRIX TITLE.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-SUSANTI WINS GRAND PRIX TITLE.

text.p: Susi Susanti won the World Grand Prix badminton title at home in Indonesia on Sunday with a convincing 11-4 11-1 victory over long-time rival Ye Zhaoying of China.

Indonesian doubles partners Ricky Subagja and Rexy Mainaky also won their final beating Cheah Soon Kit and Yap Him Hock of Malaysia 15-4 15-9 in a re-run of the Olympic final earlier this year in Atlanta.

The victories in the sport's richest tournament of the year made up for a series of earlier Indonesian disappointments with world number nine and Susanti's fiance, Allan Budi Kusuma, getting knocked out in Saturday's semifinals and defeats in both the women's and mixed doubles finals on Sunday.
World number-one Joko Suprianto had also pulled out earlier from the competition being played on the Indonesian holiday island of Bali, complaining of a leg injury.

In the men's final, Fung Permadi, formerly of Indonesia but now of Taiwan, overpowered Sun Jun of China in 49 minutes to win 15-12 15-8 after Jun slipped in the first set and had to have his knee bandaged before resuming play.
It was an important win for Permadi who is not in the top 10 of the world rankings. Jun is currently number seven.
"I'm glad I won but I'm not satisfied with my performance," Permadi said, adding he was disappointed that both Suprianto and his opponent in the final had been hampered by injury.
Susanti, number two in the world, was never troubled by Ye who consistently made unforced errors, misjudging drop-shots into the net. The match lasted only 28 minutes.
At 8-1 up in the second set, Susi looked inspired by the ebullient Indonesian crowd who met every one of her shots with a 'yeah' and booed her opponent's returns.

Susanti pocketed $17,500 of the total $65,625 prize money on offer in the women's competition and remained on top of the World Grand Prix rankings ahead of Camilla Martin of Denmark, who she beat in Saturday's semi-finals.
Permadi took home $22,750 for his win from a total pot of $96,250 in the men's competition.
